title: Write draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00.md
description:
Write the normative DID companion draft. Sized to match draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00 (~5 pages of normative text). All design decisions are locked in 8sgn.1; do not re-litigate them.

## Deliverable

`draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00.md` at the top level of the repo. IETF Internet-Draft format (kramdown-rfc2629 frontmatter + Markdown body), same shape as the seven existing drafts.

## Required sections

1. Front matter (title, abbrev, docname, author, normative refs to RFC 2119/8174/8620, DID-CORE; informative refs to JMAP-CHAT and JMAP-CHAT-FED)
2. Abstract
3. Introduction (and design philosophy: minimal wire contract, deployment-defined posture, alignment with q15f Option B in core)
4. Conventions and definitions
5. Capability
   - Session-level: `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:did`, empty object
   - Account-level: object with `supportedDidMethods` array (REQUIRED) and any other fields the draft locks
6. Mandatory DID methods (did:web, did:key, did:plc — MUST resolve and verify)
7. ChatContact extensions
   - `id` MAY be a DID URI (cross-reference q15f / commit 48b6a31 in core)
   - Optional `did` field for pseudonymous case
   - Consistency rule when both present
8. Federation authentication
   - Signature-against-DID-bound-key requirement (normative)
   - RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures + Ed25519 recommended (non-normative)
   - Components, clock skew, replay window: deployment-defined
9. DID resolution
   - Caching: impl-defined except for hard-refresh-on-verify-failure normative sentence
   - Resolution failure handling: reject auth (do not silently downgrade)
10. Mention textual form: `@{did:method:value}`
11. Security considerations
    - Key compromise and rotation
    - did:plc operation log integrity
    - did:web DNS / TLS dependency
    - did:key non-rotatability
    - Cross-method consistency
12. Federation considerations (cross-reference to the federation draft for the Peer/* method set; the DID draft only adds the auth-mechanism layer)
13. IANA considerations
    - Capability URN: `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:did`
14. Design influences and non-normative notes (mirror the pattern in calendars / tasks drafts)

## Non-goals (do not include in this draft)

- DID document conventions (auth/keyAgreement role split is Agora's, not the spec's)
- Provisioning workflows
- Recovery mechanisms
- Multi-device handling
- Trust levels
- Specific cache TTLs
- Specific replay-prevention parameters
- mTLS or OAuth+DID-claim alternative auth mechanisms

## Cross-file consistency checks before close

Per AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table:
- Capability URN string: grep all files for any prior mention
- Verify the q15f Option B prose in the core draft still permits DIDs as ChatContact.id
- Confirm no foreclosure of other DID methods anywhere in the corpus

## Acceptance criteria

- File exists with correct kramdown-rfc2629 frontmatter
- All required sections present and non-empty
- Normative size ~5 pages (comparable to tasks-00)
- No content from the explicit non-goals list
- Capability URN `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:did` registered in IANA section
- Cross-references to core draft and federation draft are correct
- README.md updated to list draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00 in both the Extensions table and the Repository Layout block (in scope for this bead; precedent set by 4nek/the README hygiene work)
- AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table extended for DID topics
close_reason: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00.md written. 299 lines, sized between filenode-00 (259) and tasks-00 (325). All sections present per 8sgn.1 design decisions: capability with supportedDidMethods array, three mandatory methods (did:web/did:key/did:plc) with open extensibility, ChatContact extensions (id-as-DID and optional did field with consistency rule), federation auth requirement with RFC 9421 as recommended realization, DID resolution caching impl-defined except for refresh-on-failure, mention textual form aligned with core draft's @did:method:value (no braces — correction recorded on 8sgn.1). Security considerations cover key compromise, did:plc log integrity, did:web DNS/TLS, did:key non-rotatability, cross-method consistency. IANA section requests capability URN registration. Explicit non-prescriptions in back-matter list all deployment-defined items (DID document conventions, multi-device, provisioning, recovery, caching parameters, signature parameters, delegation, trust levels, hardware attestation). README.md updated: Extensions table + Repository Layout. AGENTS.md updated: 'Nine drafts' sentence + cross-file consistency table extended with DID guide row. No URN conflicts across corpus. Textual mention form @did:method:value verified consistent with core draft line 293 and implementer guide lines 665/715. Not committed; awaiting user approval per project AGENTS.md restriction.
